trial_court: Court of Ms. Neena Bansal Krishna, Principal District & Sessions Judge, South East: Saket Court, New Delhi (CA No. 160/2019)
case_name: Ms. Neelam W/O Sh. Vijay Matta vs Sh. Vijay Matta S/O Sh. Manohar Lal Matta

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Ms. Neelam W/O Sh. Vijay Matta (Appellant/Complainant)
parties.respondent_defendant: Sh. Vijay Matta S/o Sh. Manohar Lal Matta (Respondent)

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Ms. Neelam got married to Sh.Vijay Matta on 21.04.2015. After the marriage, parties residing together as husband and wife. Appellant claimed Rs. 12 lacs were spent in the marriage including stridhan of about 5,50,000/- which was entrusted to the Respondent at the time of marriage.

legal_principles.principle: A person has a legal duty to maintain their minor children.
legal_principles.held: He has a legal duty to maintain his minor children from his first marriage.
applicable_acts_sections: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005 — Section 23

legal_principles.principle: A person's obligation to maintain their spouse is not limited by their own income or employment status.
legal_principles.held: Moreover, even though Appellant/Complainant is more qualified it is the obligation of the Respondent, being the husband to maintain her as she has no means to sustain herself and is presently being supported by her aged parents who are senior citizens.
applicable_acts_sections: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005 — Section 23

outcome.final_order: The application of the Appellant/Complainant for claiming interim maintenance has been set aside.
